SCGSim prepares an AEDT study on your machine, Ansys AEDT solves it, and
SCGSim reads back what it returned. This page says which AEDT versions it
drives, the one modeling choice you make (`solid` or `thin_film`), what each
calculation needs and returns, and how to stop a Q3D run or solve HFSS EPR on
another host. The guides walk through each calculation:
[capacitance with Q3D](../../guides/capacitance-q3d.qmd),
[modes with HFSS](../../guides/modes-hfss.qmd),
[S-parameters with HFSS](../../guides/s-parameters-hfss.qmd) and
[line parameters with Q2D](../../guides/line-parameters-q2d.qmd).
How the runtime works inside (record formats, readback, the junction cut) is
on [AEDT runtime internals](../../contribute/internals/aedt-runtime.qmd).

## How a run goes {#one-shared-lifecycle}

1. **Prepare.** A preparation call writes a *handoff*: a folder with the
   model, the request (`aedt_spec.json`) and a run script. Nothing is solved
   and AEDT is not started. The calls are `EigenmodeSim.prepare_handoff()`
   for HFSS Eigenmode, `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(...)` for Driven
   Terminal, `prepare_q3d_from_geometry(...)` for Q3D and
   `prepare_handoff(spec=...)` for Q2D.
2. **Run.** On a host with AEDT and its license:

   ```sh
   python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute
   ```

   The run opens its own AEDT Desktop, builds the model, solves, exports the
   results, saves the project and closes the Desktop. It writes a *receipt*,
   the record of what ran and what came out.
3. **Read.** `resolve_results(run_dir)` checks the returned folder against its
   receipt and returns a `ResolvedRun`; `show_all_results()` shows it.

A run that is missing a native result or a file the receipt names is a failed
run; SCGSim does not fill the gap. [Run a prepared model](../../guides/run-elsewhere.qmd)
covers copying a handoff to another host and back.

### AEDT version {#aedt-version-selection}

Every AEDT request and handoff takes `aedt_version="2023.2"` or
`aedt_version="2024.2"`. There is no default, and SCGSim never falls back from
one release to the other. Both use PyAEDT 1.3.0, with Python 3.12 or 3.13, and
the AEDT Desktop runs on the same host as SCGSim. The receipt records the
version AEDT reports, next to the one you asked for.

Superconductors of the PDK become perfect conductors: a solid uses AEDT's
`pec` material with Solve Inside off; a sheet is a Perfect E boundary in HFSS
and a `ThinConductor` of the film's thickness in Q3D. Every
other material uses its exact AEDT library name from the PDK; SCGSim invents no
material properties.

### Build the model without solving {#aedt-model-only-preparation}

To look at the AEDT model before you pay for a solve, prepare with
`run_control=None` and run with `--prepare-only`:

```sh
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only
```

AEDT builds the model and its assignments, reads them back, saves the project
and closes; it does not mesh or solve. Read the result with
`resolve_prepared_model(run_dir)`, which returns a `PreparedModel`. It is a
prepared model, not a result: `resolve_results()` refuses it. A later solve
needs a new handoff. This works for Q3D, HFSS Eigenmode (EPR included) and
HFSS Driven Terminal.

## Solid or thin_film {#aedt-solid-thin-film}

Every HFSS and Q3D request names `modeling="solid"` or `modeling="thin_film"`;
there is no default. The choice decides how the metal films enter the model.

- **`solid`** keeps every film as a volume of its real thickness. Use it when
  the film thickness matters to the field, or to compare with a Route B Palace
  model. (In SCGSim's geometry builder this is Route C: the conductor volumes
  stay in the model.)
- **`thin_film`** replaces each film of the layer stack by a zero-thickness
  sheet at the face it sits on, and removes the film's thickness from the
  stack, so everything above it moves down by that thickness. Bumps and posts
  stay solids. Use it to match a Route A Palace model, or when the films are
  thin next to the gaps. A thin Q3D sheet still carries the film's thickness
  as a `ThinConductor`.

For example, take a flip-chip stack with two 0.1 µm aluminium films and a
bump between them, heights in µm:

| Part | `solid` | `thin_film` |
|---|---|---|
| Bottom substrate | −500 to 0 | −500 to 0 |
| Bottom film | 0 to 0.1, a volume | a sheet at z = 0 |
| Bump | 0.1 to 10.1 | 0 to 10.0 |
| Top film | 10.1 to 10.2, a volume | a sheet at z = 10.0 |
| Top substrate | 10.2 to 510.2 | 10.0 to 510.0 |

Under `thin_film` the metal-to-metal gap stays 10.0 µm, and the two substrates
come 0.2 µm closer. The outlines, holes, materials and Net names are the same
in both. The film thickness of the model is separate from the thickness of a
Surface-EPR film (`film_thickness_m` in `plan.set_surface_epr`), which is a
loss assumption of its own. [Physical representation](physical-representation.qmd)
gives the profiles behind these two choices, and
[Route A and Route B](../../concepts/routes.qmd) explains the routes.

## What each calculation needs and returns {#solver-specific-contracts}

Every 3D calculation solves the SGB model of a `GeometryPlan` snapshot: SCGSim
builds the model Palace would mesh, writes it as a STEP file, and AEDT imports
it. Q2D takes a cross-section you describe instead.

| Calculation | You give | You get back |
|---|---|---|
| HFSS Eigenmode | The plan, `modeling`, and an `EigenmodeRunControl` with the number of modes and the lowest frequency; optionally junctions, RLCs and an EPR request | Mode frequencies, native Q and convergence; with EPR, participation per mode and pass |
| HFSS Driven Terminal | The plan, `modeling`, two lumped Terminal ports on port sheets of the plan, and an `HfssRunControl` with its frequency sweep | Terminal S-parameters as CSV and Touchstone |
| Q3D | The plan, `modeling`, the Q3D type of every Net, and a `MatrixRunControl` | The capacitance and conductance matrix (`results/q3d/c_matrix.csv`) |
| Q2D | Rectangles of the cross-section and their conductor groups, and a `MatrixRunControl` | Per-unit-length C, G, L and R in one file |

### Run controls {#aedt-family-setup-controls}

The run controls are typed records; their fields are the AEDT setup values.

| Record | Fields (defaults) | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `EigenmodeRunControl` | `setup_name`, `minimum_frequency_ghz`, `num_modes`, `maximum_passes`, `maximum_delta_frequency_percent`, `minimum_passes` (1), `minimum_converged_passes` (1), `percent_refinement` (30) | GHz; percent |
| `HfssRunControl` | `setup_name`, `sweep_name`, `sweep` (a `FrequencySweepSpec`), `maximum_passes` (99), `minimum_passes` (1), `minimum_converged_passes` (1), `percent_refinement` (30), `maximum_delta_s` (0.02) | delta-S is a ratio |
| `FrequencySweepSpec` | `start_ghz`, `stop_ghz`, `points` (20000) | GHz |
| `MatrixRunControl` | `setup_name`, `frequency_ghz`, `maximum_passes`, `convergence_percent` (1.0), `minimum_passes` (1), `minimum_converged_passes` (1), `percent_refinement` (30) | GHz; percent |
| `AedtResources` | `cores`, `ram_limit_percent` (1 to 100) | |

[]{#hfss-driven-sweep-count}`points` is the number of sweep samples you
choose. It takes a whole number, such as `20000` or `20000.0`; `20000.5` is
refused, not rounded. SCGSim reads back exactly that many points.

### Port sheets, junctions and RLCs {#hfss-shared-lumped-support}

What sits on a port sheet is the plan's: each lumped element of
`plan.set_lumped_elements` ([Lumped elements](geometry-plan.qmd#lumped-elements)),
on the sheet it names. HFSS makes of each one:

| On the plan | HFSS Eigenmode | HFSS Driven Terminal |
|---|---|---|
| `LumpedElement` with an inductance and no resistance | a junction: a Lumped RLC of its L and C (C = 0 when none is given), with junction participation; its EPR id is its sheet's name | refused, naming the element |
| any other `LumpedElement` | a parallel Lumped RLC of its R, L and C, a linear circuit element with no junction participation | refused, naming the element |
| `LumpedPort` | a parallel Lumped RLC of its impedance, a load | a lumped Terminal port, in the plan's order |

Each sheet is cut to the rectangle between its two conductors, as Palace cuts
it ([How a junction is cut](#aedt-automatic-junction-partition)). A sheet the
plan declares nothing on is not in the model.

AEDT keeps only the letters, digits and `_` of a name, so a Net named
`chip/A` becomes `chip_A` in AEDT. Two Nets whose names become the same, such
as `chip/A` and `chip_A`, are refused before AEDT starts, with both names; so
are two junctions or two RLCs whose names collide. Nothing is renamed.

### HFSS Driven Terminal {#hfss-driven-terminal-sgb}

Declare two `LumpedPort`s on the plan, with one shared reference Net, and
prepare the run with `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(plan.prepare(), modeling=..., ...)`.
Port 1 is the first `LumpedPort`; each port's AEDT name is its sheet's name
with every character other than letters, digits and `_` made `_`. Each port
sheet joins two conductors: the one in its `reference_net` is the reference,
the other the signal, where the Terminal goes. A Driven model carries no
junctions, RLCs or Surface-EPR specs: a `LumpedElement` on the plan is
refused, and the plan's Surface-EPR specs are not read. The run returns the S-parameters of the declared sweep in
port order, as CSV and as Touchstone.

Driven Modal and wave ports are not available; see [Not supported](#current-exclusions).

### HFSS Eigenmode and EPR {#eigenmode-saved-fields-and-surface-epr-direction}

`EigenmodeSim(modeling=..., aedt_version=...)` takes the plan with `set_plan`,
the setup with `set_eigenmode`, and optionally `set_epr_request`; the
junctions and lumped RLCs are the plan's lumped elements. Surface EPR is the plan's
(`plan.set_surface_epr(specs)` before `prepare()`): its inset margins are cut
into the model as bands. Every Surface-EPR row of the declared types is
integrated over all its faces, side walls included, unless the spec's
`face_kinds` leaves them out. The [HFSS modes guide](../../guides/modes-hfss.qmd) runs
the calls in order.

`EprAnalysisRequest` chooses what is reported: `surface_epr_groups` (every
group when `None`), `junction_ids` and `bulk_domain_ids`. Every domain and
junction stays in the normalization, whatever is reported.

To compute EPR again from fields AEDT saved, without solving again, use
[`analyze_epr`](../api/analyze-epr.qmd). It opens AEDT, so it needs a license.
[]{#public-epr-candidate-surface}All of these take the one `PreparedSgbModel`
of the plan (`EigenmodeSim.prepared_model`).

#### Converge on an EPR quantity {#epr-expression-cache-convergence}

By default HFSS stops refining when the mode frequencies settle
(`maximum_delta_frequency_percent`). `set_expression_cache_convergence` adds a
participation as a further criterion: AEDT then stops only when the frequency
and every selected participation change by less than their criteria. This
example asks for the MA and MS participation of mode 1 beyond the 0.5 µm
margin, each within 5 % from pass to pass:

```python
from scgsim.aedt import (
    ExpressionCacheConvergence,
    ExpressionCacheConvergenceSet,
    NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal,
)

sim.set_expression_cache_convergence(
    ExpressionCacheConvergenceSet(
        controls=(
            ExpressionCacheConvergence(
                mode=1,
                target=NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal("MA", "requested_margin", 0.5),
                criterion=5.0,
                use_relative_convergence=True,
            ),
            ExpressionCacheConvergence(
                mode=1,
                target=NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal("MS", "requested_margin", 0.5),
                criterion=5.0,
                use_relative_convergence=True,
            ),
        )
    )
)
```

[]{#independent-expression-cache-convergence-targets}The EPR request must
report that mode and that margin. Each target is its own criterion; they are
never summed. With `use_relative_convergence=True` the criterion is AEDT's
**Max Percent Delta** in percent (`5.0` is 5 %); with `False` it is **Max
Delta** in the quantity's own units. Pass one `ExpressionCacheConvergence` for
a single target, or `None` for none. A `NativeExpressionDefinition` target
takes your own Fields Calculator steps instead of a participation. AEDT
documents the rule in its
[expression convergence reference](https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/public/Views/Secured/Electronics/v242/en/Subsystems/HFSS/Content/HFSS/SpecifyingExpressionsforAdaptiveConvergence.htm).

#### How a junction is cut {#aedt-automatic-junction-partition}

AEDT puts a junction's inductance on a rectangle, and every other lumped
element on the same kind of rectangle. SCGSim cuts the drawn sheet into two
conductor ends, each joined to its terminal, and one
full-width central rectangle that carries the whole inductance and
capacitance. The sheet must have a clear full-width corridor between its two
terminals, touching no other metal; otherwise preparation stops and names the
junction. The cut rule and its checks are in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-automatic-junction-partition).

![The drawn sheet and the prepared pieces: the existing A and B terminals (pale), the added conductor ends (darker) and the central RLC rectangle.](../../assets/junction-partition-generic.svg){fig-alt="Generic authored sheet with pale existing terminal metal, darker added conductor ends, and the central RLC rectangle." width="95%"}

### Q3D {#q3d-sgb-model}

[]{#q3d-extraction-and-region-ground-candidate}`prepare_q3d_from_geometry(snapshot, ...)`
takes the snapshot, `modeling`, the Q3D type of every Net (`net_types`, keyed
by Net ID: `"Signal"` or `"Ground"`) and the Nets that are physically ground
(`physical_ground_nets`); the [Q3D guide](../../guides/capacitance-q3d.qmd)
shows the call. The plan needs a vacuum region: Q3D's Region is the plan's
vacuum box. Q3D extracts C and G only.

`Q3dSpec.grounded_region_net` chooses the outer boundary; it is a field of a
`Q3dSpec` you build and pass to `prepare_handoff`, and
`prepare_q3d_from_geometry` leaves it `None`. `None` leaves the Region open.
A name makes SCGSim cover the six faces of the Region with
perfect-conductor sheets assigned to a new ground Net of that name, which must
not be the name of a Net of the model.

### Q2D {#q2d-native-combined-matrix-export}

A Q2D run returns one file, `results/q2d/rlgc_matrix.csv`, with the
per-unit-length capacitance (C), conductance (G), inductance (L) and
resistance (R) matrices; `result.physics_results()` gives its rows.

## Convergence is recorded, not judged {#hfss-convergence-observations}

[]{#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations}SCGSim records what AEDT reports for
every adaptive run: whether it converged, the target, the last change and the
passes. It does not fail a run because the last change is above your target,
or because it ended at a pass count other than your maximum. A real failure
stays a failure: a crash, a solve that ran out of memory or time, a failed
save, a missing or damaged file. Whether the result is good enough for your
study is your judgement; [Convergence and reports](../../guides/convergence-and-reports.qmd)
shows how to read it.

## Stop or abort a Q3D run {#q3d-user-requested-stopabort-and-save}

A long Q3D solve can be ended early and saved, from another process on the
same Linux host:

- `scgsim.aedt.request_q3d_stop_and_save(handoff)` asks AEDT for a clean stop:
  the current pass finishes;
- `scgsim.aedt.request_q3d_abort_and_save(handoff)` aborts the current work.

From the command line:

```sh
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --stop-and-save
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --abort-and-save
```

Run one of them while the run started with `--execute` is solving; the two
cannot be combined. When AEDT has
stopped and the project is saved, the receipt status is `normal_stop_saved` or
`abort_saved`. That is a saved project, not a finished solve:
`resolve_results()` does not read it as a result. If SCGSim cannot confirm
that AEDT stopped, or the save fails, the run fails and the Desktop is left
open for you.

[]{#q3d-native-build-only-execution}A Q3D handoff can also be built without
solving, as in [Build the model without solving](#aedt-model-only-preparation).

## Solve HFSS EPR on another host {#prepared-native-hfss-epr-batch}

An HFSS EPR study can be solved by AEDT's batch solver on a host without a
Desktop session, for example a compute node. It has three steps on two kinds
of host:

| Step | Host | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| Package | Your workstation with SCGSim and AEDT | A prepare-only EPR run folder |
| Solve | The solver host | The same AEDT release, its command-line solver and a license; no SCGSim, no PyAEDT |
| Collect | Your workstation | The returned package and attempt, complete |

```sh
# 1. Package one prepared model (workstation).
python -m scgsim.aedt.batch package \
  --prepared-run "$PREPARED_RUN" --output "$PACKAGE_DIR" \
  --solver-executable "$AEDT_SOLVER" --cores "$AEDT_CORES" \
  --ram-limit-percent "$AEDT_RAM_LIMIT_PERCENT"

# 2. Solve (solver host; the package's own script needs only Python).
python "$PACKAGE_DIR/run_batch.py" solve \
  --package "$PACKAGE_DIR" --output "$ATTEMPT_DIR"

# 3. Collect the full adaptive history and saved-field EPR (workstation).
python -m scgsim.aedt.batch collect \
  --package "$PACKAGE_DIR" --attempt "$ATTEMPT_DIR" \
  --output "$COLLECTED_RUN_DIR"
```

`--cores` is a positive whole number and `--ram-limit-percent` a whole number
from 1 to 99; `--dependency` may be repeated. The same steps are Python calls:
`prepare_native_batch`, `run_native_batch` and `collect_native_batch`. Bring
back the whole package and attempt, with the `.aedt` project and its
`.aedtresults` folder; a frequency export alone cannot be collected. One
package holds one model; [AEDT: parameter sweep on HPC](../../guides/hpc-sweep.qmd)
runs many.

## Time and memory of a run {#native-simulation-benchmark}

Every completed AEDT solve records the times, memory and mesh sizes AEDT
reports for each stage and pass. `ResolvedRun.show_simulation_benchmark(theme="light")`
shows them as cards, a table and, where AEDT reports adaptive values, curves;
`theme="dark"` suits a dark notebook. A value AEDT does not report stays
missing, never zero. AEDT reports memory per task, so a peak is the largest
task's, not the whole host's.

## How EPR is normalized {#surface-estimates-and-junction-normalization}

The energy participation of a part of the model is its energy divided by one
normalization energy $U_{norm}$: the electric energy in every solution domain,
$U_E=\epsilon_0/2\sum_D\int_D\epsilon_r|E|^2dV$, plus the capacitive energy of
every junction, $U_{norm}=U_E+\sum_j U_{C,j}$. The thin-film surface energies
are estimated from the field at the surface and are not added to
$U_{norm}$. With peak phasors, film thickness $t$, film relative permittivity
$\epsilon_f$ and substrate relative permittivity $\epsilon_s$:

$$
U_{MA}=\frac{\epsilon_0 t}{2\epsilon_f}\int |E_{n,air}|^2\,dA,
\quad
U_{MS}=\frac{\epsilon_0 t\epsilon_s^2}{2\epsilon_f}
\int |E_{n,substrate}|^2\,dA,
$$

$$
U_{SA}=\frac{\epsilon_0 t}{2}\int
\left(\epsilon_f|E_{t,air}|^2+\frac{|E_{n,air}|^2}{\epsilon_f}\right)dA.
$$

A junction's voltage is the field along its direction, averaged over the
width $w$ of its sheet, with $\hat{\ell}$ the unit vector from terminal A to B:

$$
V=\frac{1}{w}\int_{sheet}E\!\cdot\!\hat{\ell}\,dA.
$$

With the convention $e^{+i\omega t}$ and $\omega=2\pi\operatorname{Re}(f)$,
$I_L=V/(i\omega L)$, $U_L=L|I_L|^2/2$ and $U_C=C|V|^2/2$; the participations
$p_L=U_L/U_{norm}$ and $p_C=U_C/U_{norm}$ are not negative. For $V\neq0$ the
effective modal capacitance is $C_{mode}=2U_{norm}/|V|^2$, the branch
capacitance $C_j=2U_{C,j}/|V|^2$, and $p_{C,j}=C_j/C_{mode}$; at $V=0$ the ratio
is undefined. [Surface EPR](../../concepts/surface-epr.qmd) explains how to
read these numbers.

## Results of an earlier SCGSim {#current-formats}

SCGSim reads only the formats it writes. A handoff, receipt or result written
by an earlier SCGSim is refused with a message saying so; read it with the
SCGSim version that wrote it, or prepare and run the study again. Run folders
of the AEDT builder that SCGSim had before it imported the SGB model are
refused the same way. []{#runtime-source}Each receipt names the SCGSim files
that ran and their hashes; the formats are listed in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/aedt-runtime.qmd#current-formats).

## Not supported {#current-exclusions}

- HFSS Driven Modal and Driven Terminal wave ports: a request with one is
  refused. They are tracked in [issue #135](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/135).
- Q3D AC/RL: Q3D extracts C and G only. Tracked in
  [issue #265](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/265).
- S-parameter circuit models, automatic choice of the solver, and AEDT
  material definitions of your own.

[]{#hfss-eigenmode-native-frequency-export}[]{#mode-binding-and-pass-cache}How
HFSS mode frequencies are read and how modes are bound in field evaluation are
on [the internals page](../../contribute/internals/aedt-runtime.qmd#hfss-eigenmode-native-frequency-export).
[Preview the geometry](../../guides/preview-the-geometry.qmd) shows the AEDT
model before you run it.
